title: Critical VMware vCenter Directory Traversal Flaw Used in Global Attacks
content_md: Broadcom VMware vCenter administrators are facing an intrusion campaign targeting CVE-2026-59310 , a critical directory-traversal vulnerability in the vCenter Syslog Server. Threat researchers at QUIRSO said they identified 361 unique victim IP addresses across 47 countries, with evidence suggesting a suspected advanced persistent threat is using the flaw to obtain code execution and establish remote access. The campaign shows attackers rapidly operationalizing weaknesses in exposed virtualization-management infrastructure. Broadcom issued advisory VMSA-2026-0006 on July 29, 2026. Critical VMware vCenter Directory Traversal Flaw QUIRSO observed affected systems begin connecting to attacker-controlled infrastructure on August 3 five calendar days later. Activity then accelerated: 151 additional victim IPs appeared on August 4, and 343 of the 361 observed addresses, roughly 95%, had been seen by August 5. CVE-2026-59310 carries a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8. The issue is a path-traversal flaw in vCenter’s Syslog Server that a network-reachable attacker can exploit to execute arbitrary code. Its risk is amplified by vCenter’s role as the management plane for virtualized environments; a compromise can give an intruder a foothold from which to target hosted workloads, credentials, or administrative operations.
